priority_note: Energy affordability stress is likely to burden households with least capacity to adapt.
Heat health emergencies disproportionately affect older residents and people with chronic illness.
Labor exposure risk is shaped by employer rules and weak worker bargaining power.
Adaptation legitimacy depends on whether exposed communities shape decisions.
Automated decision failures may create severe due-process barriers.
Workers may absorb accountability for systems they do not control.
Trust losses are concentrated among people already harmed by public-service failures.
Legal pressure may follow unequal service harms and appeal failures.
